regions.label: Figure B5.1.2 — Major wage differentials for ICT professionals create a brain drain, especially in low- and middle-income countries
regions.summary: Two bar charts compare net worker flows with disruptive technology skills and mean nominal monthly ICT earnings across four income groups. High-income countries show positive net flows and much higher earnings; the other groups show negative net flows and lower earnings.
regions.details: Panel a, “Net flow of workers with disruptive technology skills”: vertical axis is net flow (per 10,000 workers), from −200 to 200; a dashed horizontal line marks zero. Categories, in order: High-income, Upper-middle-income, Lower-middle-income, Low-income. Approximate bar values read from the chart: +120, −180, −160, and −135, respectively. Panel b, “Mean nominal monthly earnings of ICT employees”: vertical axis is earnings (US$), from 0 to 4,000 in 500 increments. The same income-group order has approximate bars of US$3,450, US$850, US$280, and US$270. No legend is shown. Source note cites ILOSTAT and LinkedIn data (2015–19); the note defines “disruptive technology skills” and expands ICT as information and communication technology.
regions.limitations: Bar values are approximate readings from the plotted heights; exact values are not printed. The chart provides no explicit data labels.
